runtime_architecture.fighting_style_data: RE4Constants.FeatureMetadata.FightingStyleCatalog is the canonical source for basic Dark Step/Electric/Water Kung Fu metadata. RE4Constants.FightingStyleRegistry derives those entries from the top-level catalog and owns Sea availability, action remote/args, safe ownership probe, dealer identity/location and requirements for both Progress and Items.
runtime_architecture.fighting_style_action: Progress consumes the shared registry for Not Owned -> Buy/Learn; Items consumes it for confirmed Owned -> Equip/Relearn. Items tries the registry action directly only after ownership is confirmed, verifies the live equipped style, then acquires Movement and uses the same dealer resolver as Progress only when needed.
runtime_architecture.fighting_style_dealer_resolution: shared registry NPC/location -> live/template NPC resolver -> shared TeleportDirectory -> exact per-Sea/style cache -> island anchor only as bootstrap -> exact dealer rescan
runtime_architecture.dealer_anchor_policy: WorldTopology island anchors are never cached or treated as dealer positions
runtime_architecture.items_use_auto_buy: false; Items rejects not_owned before any action remote or Movement acquisition
runtime_architecture.items_fighting_equip_mount: RE4StyleProgress is release-scoped, then RE4StyleProgress:MountUseControls(RE4Tabs.Items) mounts controls into the current window; stale UseUI.Mounted state is not reused across builds
runtime_architecture.bisento_v2_requirements: Own Bisento V1 + personally deal >=10% of Greybeard max HP + Greybeard defeat; Bisento equip not required
runtime_architecture.bisento_v2_confirmation: event-driven PlayerGui upgrade-message capture + explicit inventory/live variant evidence + bounded post-kill verification
runtime_architecture.fighting_style_sea_source: RE4Ownership:Sea() is the shared current-Sea resolver. The ownership service reads RE4RuntimeContext.Core.SeaNumber as authoritative state with World1/World2/World3 only as fallback; RefreshStyleServer and RE4StyleProgress both consume the same exported ownership service instead of a cross-domain local helper.
runtime_architecture.items_fighting_equip_visibility: Items Fighting rows are mounted by current-Sea registry availability and then shown only on confirmed shared ownership. Basic registry metadata is validated before runtime; dealer/NPC replication is never consulted for visibility and is resolved only after an owned style is selected for Equip when direct relearn is unverified.
runtime_architecture.second_sea_access: Level 700+ -> Military Detective -> Key -> live Frozen Village door -> Ice Admiral -> return Military Detective -> Experienced Captain -> TravelDressrosa
runtime_architecture.second_sea_npc_resolution: shared RE4TeleportDirectory exact live/template NPC target; WorldTopology island anchor is bootstrap-only while NPC is unresolved
runtime_architecture.second_sea_state_policy: monotonic worker state; Ice Admiral Humanoid.Died/progression completion advances post-boss flow and prevents rollback to the door step
runtime_architecture.dealer_required_policy: Dealer state is resolved only when an owned style is actually requested for Equip/Relearn and direct equip is unverified/unsupported. Dealer replication never participates in Items ownership or visibility.
runtime_architecture.fighting_style_ownership: Shared RE4Ownership evidence pipeline: current live/container state + raw inventory/mastery index + replicated player/unlockable state + registry-declared read-only ownership probes + data-driven prerequisite proof. Basic Fighting Styles inherit an explicit {true} ownership probe from RE4BuildBasicStyleMeta using the catalog remote; positive result 1 is sticky ownership evidence, while ambiguous/non-positive values remain Unknown unless NegativeAuthoritative is explicitly declared.

root_cause: Basic Fighting Style data existed twice (FightingStyleCatalog and literal StyleMeta fields), creating drift risk.

Exact dealer targets resolved during Progression were not retained. If the NPC/template became temporarily unresolvable during Items Equip, MoveDealer degraded to the generic island anchor and could end with dealer_not_loaded.

notes: 2.0.20 makes FightingStyleRegistry the single runtime data source for Progress and Items rather than maintaining separate ownership/action/dealer tables.
Ownership is fail-closed: no prerequisite/upgrade inference is used to make a style visible in Items; only live/inventory evidence or the style own server ownership probe can confirm it.

Direct Equip/Relearn is treated as a runtime capability attempt, not assumed from a return value. Success requires the live equipped style to change; otherwise Items falls back to the shared dealer route.

No new scheduler, Heartbeat/Stepped listener or background task was added. No live Roblox runtime is available in the build container, so remote acceptance/NPC streaming must still be smoke-tested in game.

2.0.21 fixes the BOOT 05 Fighting Style crash at its domain-boundary root cause: Progression no longer references the core-local RE4OwnershipSea helper; current Sea is resolved through the exported RE4Ownership service.

2.0.22 fixes Items Fighting Style visibility at ownership-source level: verified positive evidence is preserved across equip switches; positive mastery/replicated data is consumed without new remotes; explicitly safe status probes are separate from action remotes; dealer replication remains irrelevant until Equip is requested.

Static 2.0.22 regression suite: 65/65 PASS. No Luau runtime/compiler is installed in the build container, so in-game remote return semantics and live replicated data still require smoke testing on Roblox.

2.0.23 identifies the remaining Items regression from the project baseline itself: the three basic {true} ownership probes present in 2.0.19 were lost when the basic registry builder set OwnershipProbe=nil. They are restored through the shared builder, not through per-style UI logic.

Static 2.0.23 regression suite: 75/75 PASS, including Sea 2 availability, shared registry probe contract, Items ownership-only visibility, direct-before-dealer Equip ordering, raw inventory-key/mastery indexing simulations, scope preservation and unchanged background/callsite counts. Live Roblox remote behavior still requires smoke testing in game.

update_2_0_15.root_cause: ui.lua suppressed the Fighting Style · Equip source section and rerouted its Use/Equip controls into curated Fighting Style sub-sections. Runtime equip logic remained in main.lua, but the expected Items section disappeared from presentation.

root_cause: The Fighting Style Equip controls were mounted from the First Sea Shop initialization path rather than from the RE4StyleProgress domain that owns StartUse/StartDealerAction. This made the expected Items section dependent on unrelated shop/presentation bootstrap behavior even though the equip runtime still existed.

Bisento V2 detection treated absence of explicit variant fields as Unknown and the old automation did not model Greybeard personal damage eligibility or capture the server upgrade notification, so the flow could kill Greybeard without ever reaching a confirmed V2 state.

fix.bisento_upgrade_notification_watcher: FeatureRuntime token-owned DescendantAdded connection; cleaned on OFF/restart
fix.post_kill_verification: bounded 3.5s; at most one forced inventory probe per second

update_2_0_17.root_cause: 2.0.16 introduced BisentoV2SessionConfirmed/Evidence reads through RE4State, but this release architecture has no RE4State variable. ResolveBisentoVariant is called by early UI ownership refresh in the core domain, before progression initialization, causing BOOT 05 to abort with attempt to index nil.

root_cause: The direct Items Fighting Style mount introduced in 2.0.16 rendered every style in every Sea, while StartDealerAction still rejected out-of-Sea metadata with wrong_sea.

RE4StyleProgress derived its Sea from cross-domain World1/World2/World3 globals instead of consuming an authoritative value exported by the Core domain, making the Use/Equip gate more fragile than the Progression/UI foundation.

RE4StyleProgress used RE4StyleProgress = RE4StyleProgress or {...}; when a newer build was executed in the same server, stale UseUI.Mounted=true caused MountUseControls to return early, so Items showed no Fighting Style Equip controls.

Auto Quest Sea 2 treated Frozen Village door state as the whole progression state. After Ice Admiral it could call TravelDressrosa without returning to Military Detective or resolving Experienced Captain, and boss/map streaming could make the worker fall back to an earlier branch.

Progress and Items consumed overlapping but different Fighting Style ownership/action data. RefreshStyleServer maintained its own remote list and inferred older style ownership from upgraded styles, while Items could resolve/equip through a different path than Progress.

Items mounted Sea-available styles even when ownership was not confirmed, so presentation and action gating could diverge. Equip also moved to the dealer before proving that an owned style could be relearned directly.

fix.direct_equip_policy: owned-only; invoke registry action; require live equipped-style confirmation
fix.dealer_fallback_policy: acquire Movement only after direct equip is unverified; resolve the same registry dealer used by Progress

root_cause: RE4OwnershipSea was declared local inside the Core initialization domain, but RE4InitProgression runs in a separate function scope. S.Sea referenced RE4OwnershipSea directly, so Luau resolved it as a missing global at Progress/Items mount and raised attempt to call a nil value.
The same current-Sea concept therefore crossed a runtime-domain boundary without being exported through RE4RuntimeContext.Core.

2.0.20 correctly removed the old hardcoded upgraded-style ownership inference, but the replacement ownership service still had no durable positive evidence path for a learned basic Fighting Style after it was no longer the equipped Tool.

RefreshStyleServer and S.CheckOwned reused Fighting Style action remotes with {true}/OwnershipArgs as if every style exposed the same ownership-query protocol. That contract is not uniform; Unknown or unrelated status results caused Items to hide owned styles because Items intentionally fails closed.

Progress and Items consumed the same resolver, but unknown ownership was asymmetric: Progress treated it as a candidate while Items hid it, allowing a style to appear lost from Items even though dealer availability was not involved.

fix.non_positive_probe_default: Unknown unless registry explicitly declares NegativeAuthoritative

root_cause: The 2.0.19 ownership service explicitly probed BuyBlackLeg(true), BuyElectro(true) and BuyFishmanKarate(true) for Sea 1-3. During the registry unification, RE4BuildBasicStyleMeta set OwnershipProbe=nil, so those three established ownership checks were silently dropped while advanced styles kept their probes.

An unequipped learned basic style therefore depended only on passive Backpack/Character/inventory/mastery/replicated evidence. If those sources did not expose historical Fighting Style ownership, Resolve returned Unknown and Items correctly hid the owned-only row.
The inventory cache also flattened dictionary-keyed server records before Reindex and did not recognize MasteryLevel-only records, weakening the passive fallback path further.

fix.ambiguous_nonpositive_result: Unknown unless NegativeAuthoritative is explicitly declared

root_cause: RE4BuildBasicStyleMeta read RE4Constants.FeatureMetadata.GameData.FightingStyleCatalog, but FightingStyleCatalog is defined directly under RE4Constants.FeatureMetadata.

Because the lookup returned {}, Dark Step/Electric/Water Kung Fu were built with nil Style/Display/Remote and Seas={}, so S.Allowed filtered them before ownership resolution and before the Items diagnostic line. This exactly matches the user log containing only advanced styles.

fix.basic_metadata_invariant: Style + Display + Remote + non-empty Seas required
fix.equip_policy: confirmed owned -> direct action -> live equipped verification -> dealer fallback
